extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the GAP computer algebra system (people implementing or using GAP vector-space, basis, linear-mapping, tensor, and algebra functionality).
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual specifications for GAP functions and filters that define properties, behaviors, and construction rules for bases, mutable bases, Gaussian/vector/matrix spaces, linear mappings, tensor/exterior/symmetric powers, and algebras. Includes definitions, return values, and implementation hooks for 'nice basis' delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal basis invariance (IsNormalBasis / NormalBasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: NormalBasis returns true if B is invariant under the Galois group of the field extension F/S, and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GaloisGroup (58.3.1). Example: CanonicalBasis( GaussianRationals ) tested with IsIntegralBasis and IsNormalBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutable vs immutable bases distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutable bases are GAP objects that are mutable (cannot store attribute values) and differ from immutable bases which store the underlying left module; both allow querying basis vectors and coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutable bases are useful when successively closing with new vectors to avoid creating new modules. Immutable produces an immutable copy of any GAP object, but here mutable bases discussed are truly mutable GAP objects and hence unable to store attribute values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of mutable bases
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP supports three kinds of mutable bases: (1) generic mutable basis that stores an immutable basis, (2) mutable bases that store a mutable basis for a 'nicer' module (useful when computations invariant under closures), and (3) mutable bases that use special information for specific types (e.g., Gaussian row and matrix spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic mutable basis when reasonable effort allows a genuinely mutable implementation. The 'nice' mutable basis approach is meaningful only if the mechanism for computing nice/ugly vectors is invariant under closures; examples include matrices, Lie objects, or elements of structure-constants algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMutableBasis filter
rubrics_metrics.description: Every mutable basis lies in the category IsMutableBasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to recognize objects that are mutable bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: MutableBasis operation
rubrics_metrics.description: MutableBasis(R, vectors[, zero]) returns a mutable basis for the R-free module generated by vectors. The optional zero is required if vectors is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that vectors will in general not be the basis vectors of the returned mutable basis. Example: MutableBasis( Rationals, [ [1,2,3], [0,1,0] ] ) returns '<mutable basis over Rationals, 2 vectors>'.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrBasisVectors behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: NrBasisVectors(MB) returns the current number of basis vectors of a mutable basis MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operation is not an attribute (value not stored). It is mainly an equivalent of Dimension for the underlying left module in the case of immutable bases. Example: NrBasisVectors can change as MB is modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImmutableBasis operation
rubrics_metrics.description: ImmutableBasis(MB[, V]) returns the immutable basis B with the same basis vectors as the mutable basis MB. If V is given it is used as the UnderlyingLeftModule for B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second variant is used when one knows a nicer module for the desired basis in advance (e.g., an algebra). Example: ImmutableBasis( MB ) can yield a SemiEchelonBasis printed representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsContainedInSpan test
rubrics_metrics.description: IsContainedInSpan(MB, v) returns true if vector v lies in the R-span of the current basis vectors of mutable basis MB, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to check membership relative to a mutable basis' current span. Example usage shown in manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: CloseMutableBasis semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: CloseMutableBasis(MB, v) changes MB so that afterwards it describes the R-span of the former basis vectors together with v; returns true if MB was extended, false if v already lay in the span.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When v enlarges the dimension, v is usually not simply appended; a linear combination of v and existing basis vectors may be added and old basis vectors may be modified (e.g., to keep list echelonized). Example sequence shows IsContainedInSpan and repeated CloseMutableBasis calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRowSpace definition
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRowSpace(V) indicates V is a vector space that consists of row vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 23 for row vector details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMatrixSpace definition
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMatrixSpace(V) indicates V is a vector space that consists of matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 24 for matrix details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGaussianSpace filter / criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGaussianSpace(V) is true for a row or matrix space V over a field F whose entries of all row vectors or matrices are contained in F; such V is called a Gaussian vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bases for Gaussian spaces can be computed using Gaussian elimination for a given list of generators. Changing entries to extension field elements can change IsGaussianSpace.

rubrics_metrics.name: FullRowSpace construction
rubrics_metrics.description: FullRowSpace(F, n) or F^n returns the F-vector space consisting of all row vectors of length n with entries in F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative constructor: F^n. Example: FullRowSpace( GF(9), 3 ) equals ( GF(3^2)^3 ).

rubrics_metrics.name: FullMatrixSpace construction
rubrics_metrics.description: FullMatrixSpace(F, m, n) or F^[m,n] returns the F-vector space of all m-by-n matrices with entries in F. If m=n the result is an algebra (FullMatrixAlgebra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative constructor: F^[m,n]. Example: FullMatrixSpace( GF(2), 4, 5 ) printed form shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: DimensionOfVectors attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: DimensionOfVectors(M) returns the common length of row vectors in left module M, or the common matrix dimensions for matrix modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For GF(2)^5 returns 5; for GF(2)^[2,3] returns [2,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSemiEchelonized property
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSemiEchelonized(B) indicates B is a semi-echelonized basis of a Gaussian row or matrix space V: for row spaces each row's first nonzero element is 1 and entries directly below pivots are 0; for matrix spaces use concatenation-of-rows criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates to SemiEchelonMat and SemiEchelonMats; examples show true/false cases for small GF(2) bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: SemiEchelonBasis behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: SemiEchelonBasis(V[, vectors]) returns a basis of V with IsSemiEchelonized property; if vectors provided and form a semi-echelonized basis of V it returns that basis, otherwise fail. SemiEchelonBasisNC does the same but omits checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called without vectors generates a semi-echelonized basis. Example shows printing BasisVectors and Coefficients and that invalid provided vectors produce fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCanonicalBasisFullRowModule criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCanonicalBasisFullRowModule(B) returns true if B is the canonical basis of a full row module: the unique semi-echelonized basis whose pivots are ordered so pivot of row j is at a larger position than pivot of row i for j>i, and each pivot column contains exactly one nonzero entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines a canonical choice for Gaussian row spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCanonicalBasisFullMatrixModule criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCanonicalBasisFullMatrixModule(B) returns true if B is the canonical basis of a full matrix module: unique semi-echelonized basis whose list of concatenated rows forms the canonical basis of the corresponding Gaussian row space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel to the full row module canonical basis definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: NormedRowVectors attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: NormedRowVectors(V) for a finite Gaussian row space V returns the list of nonzero vectors in V that have a one in their first nonzero component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result can be used as action domain for OnLines to obtain natural action on one-dimensional subspaces (useful for group actions). Example shows Action( GL(2,3), vecs, OnLines ).

rubrics_metrics.name: SiftedVector operation
rubrics_metrics.description: SiftedVector(B, v) returns the residuum of v with respect to a semi-echelonized basis B obtained by cleaning pivot positions via subtracting multiples of basis vectors; result is zero iff v lies in V. B may be a mutable basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as membership/residuum computation. Example: SiftedVector( B, [1,2,8] ) yields [0,0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftModuleGeneralMappingByImages semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftModuleGeneralMappingByImages(V, W, gens, imgs) returns the general mapping from V to W mapping gens to imgs and taking the R-linear closure; gens need not generate V and the result may be multi-valued (hence not a mapping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification doesn't define a single-valued linear map the result will be multi-valued; use IsMapping to check. Example demonstrates IsMapping(f) false.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftModuleHomomorphismByImages semantics and checks
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftModuleHomomorphismByImages(V, W, gens, imgs) returns the left R-module homomorphism mapping gens to imgs; returns fail if gens do not generate V or if the homomorphism does not exist. LeftModuleHomomorphismByImagesNC omits checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LeftModuleGeneralMappingByImages to create possibly multi-valued additive/scalar-respecting mappings. Example shows creation and Image application.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftModuleHomomorphismByMatrix construction
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftModuleHomomorphismByMatrix(BS, matrix, BR) returns the R-linear mapping from V to W defined by matrix: the image of the i-th basis vector of BS is the linear combination of BR's basis vectors with coefficients the i-th row of matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BS and BR are bases of the source and target left R-modules respectively. Example shows printed mapping by matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: NaturalHomomorphismBySubspace
rubrics_metrics.description: NaturalHomomorphismBySubspace(V, W) returns the R-linear mapping that is the natural projection of V onto the factor space V/W when W is a subspace of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: NaturalHomomorphismBySubspace( Rationals^3, W ) returns a linear mapping by matrix to Rationals^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hom(F, V, W) returns the F-vector space of all F-linear mappings from V to W (viewing V and W as F-modules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimension(Hom) yields dimension of linear map space (example: Dimension(H) = 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: End operation
rubrics_metrics.description: End(F, V) returns the F-algebra of all F-linear mappings from V to V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: End( Rationals, Rationals^2 ) has Dimension 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFullHomModule property
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFullHomModule(M) indicates M is a module of all R-linear mappings between two left R-modules; Hom can construct such a module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IsFullHomModule( Hom(Rationals, V, W) ) returns true.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPseudoCanonicalBasisFullHomModule criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPseudoCanonicalBasisFullHomModule(B) returns true if a basis B of a full hom module is pseudo canonical: matrices of its basis vectors (w.r.t. stored bases of source and range) contain exactly one identity entry and otherwise zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This depends on stored bases and is not a canonical basis in the prior sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLinearMappingsModule filter and delegation format
rubrics_metrics.description: If V is in IsLinearMappingsModule then V consists of linear mappings and is handled via the mechanism of nice bases: NiceFreeLeftModuleInfo value of V is a record with components basissource and basisrange, and NiceVector value of v is defined as the matrix of v w.r.t those bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables representing linear maps as matrices in the 'nice' free left module for efficient computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NiceFreeLeftModule attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: NiceFreeLeftModule(V) stores the associated free left module W to which tasks for V are delegated when handled via nice bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to implement delegation of computations to a nicer module, typically a row module.

rubrics_metrics.name: NiceVector / UglyVector bijection contract
rubrics_metrics.description: NiceVector(V, v) and UglyVector(V, r) provide the linear bijection between V and W := NiceFreeLeftModule(V). NiceVector returns fail or an element of W's family; UglyVector returns fail or element of V's family. If v ∈ V then UglyVector(V, NiceVector(V, v)) = v; if r ∈ W then NiceVector(V, UglyVector(V, r)) = r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows delegating membership tests and other operations in V to the corresponding operations in W.

rubrics_metrics.name: NiceFreeLeftModuleInfo attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: NiceFreeLeftModuleInfo(V) must provide the information (if any) necessary for NiceVector and UglyVector to translate between V and its NiceFreeLeftModule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing a new handled module, this attribute provides additional data needed for the bijection.

rubrics_metrics.name: NiceBasis attribute behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: NiceBasis(B) for a basis B handled via nice bases yields the basis C of NiceFreeLeftModule(V) corresponding to B: if B has no stored basis vectors, NiceBasis(B) = Basis(NiceFreeLeftModule(V)); otherwise it is Basis(NiceFreeLeftModule(V), NiceVector of B's vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is fail iff stored 'basis vectors' in B are not actually basis vectors. GeneratorsOfLeftModule correspondence is maintained via NiceVector/UglyVector.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBasisByNiceBasis filter
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBasisByNiceBasis(B) indicates B delegates tasks such as computation of coefficients to a basis of an isomorphic 'nicer' free left module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks bases that act as wrappers delegating computations to NiceBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsHandledByNiceBasis filter
rubrics_metrics.description: IsHandledByNiceBasis(M) indicates the free left module M is handled via the mechanism of nice bases, meaning essentially all operations are performed using a 'nicer' free left module (usually a row module).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modules in this category store NiceFreeLeftModule and related info for delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare/InstallHandlingByNiceBasis implementation contract
rubrics_metrics.description: DeclareHandlingByNiceBasis(name, info) and InstallHandlingByNiceBasis(name, record) register a new kind of free left modules to be handled via nice bases. record must contain detect, NiceFreeLeftModuleInfo, NiceVector, UglyVector implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: name becomes a filter f that implies IsFreeLeftModule; an implication to IsHandledByNiceBasis is installed. The pair [f, record.detect] is added to NiceBasisFiltersInfo and LeftModuleByGenerators methods call CheckForHandlingByNiceBasis to set appropriate filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: NiceBasisFiltersInfo global registry
rubrics_metrics.description: NiceBasisFiltersInfo is a global list overviewing all kinds of vector spaces currently handled by nice bases (pairs of filter and detect functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include vector spaces of field elements (but not fields themselves) and non-Gaussian row/matrix spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: CheckForHandlingByNiceBasis usage
rubrics_metrics.description: CheckForHandlingByNiceBasis(R, gens, M, zero) should be called whenever a free left module is constructed for which IsHandledByNiceBasis may be useful. It uses R (coefficient ring), gens (generators), M (constructed module), and zero element (or false if gens nonempty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This call sets appropriate filters for the module if applicable; it is used in VectorSpaceByGenerators, AlgebraByGenerators, IdealByGenerators, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: TensorProduct construction and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: TensorProduct(list) or TensorProduct(V, W, ...) returns the tensor product of vector spaces (must share same field). Elements are linear combinations of v1 ⊗ ... ⊗ vk printed as v_1<x> ... <x>v_k; zero printed as '<0-tensor>'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zeros of different tensor products have different families. Example: TensorProduct(Rationals^2, Rationals^3) yields vector space with 6 generators and a Basis listing with printed tensor elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ExteriorPower construction and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: ExteriorPower(V, k) returns the k-th exterior power whose elements are linear combinations of vi1 ∧ ... ∧ vik (1 ≤ i1 < ... < ik) and wedge elements are printed as v_1/\ ... /\v_k; zero printed as '<0-wedge>'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zeros of different exterior powers have different families. Example: ExteriorPower(Rationals^3, 2) and its Basis are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricPower construction
rubrics_metrics.description: SymmetricPower(V, k) returns the k-th symmetric power of vector space V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SymmetricPower(Rationals^3, 2) yields vector space with 6 generators and Basis printed using dot-product notation for symmetric tensors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebra constructor semantics (Algebra)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebra(F, gens[, zero][, 'basis']) constructs the algebra over division ring F generated by gens. If zero provided, uses that zero element; if final arg is 'basis' it is assumed gens form a basis of the algebra as an F-vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimension and other algebra functions apply. Example: Algebra( Rationals, [m] ) yields an algebra and Dimension(A) returns its dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: AlgebraWithOne constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AlgebraWithOne(F, gens[, zero][, 'basis']) constructs an algebra-with-one over division ring F generated by gens; optional zero and 'basis' behave analogously to Algebra. One(A) returns identity when present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: One(A) printed for AlgebraWithOne(Rationals,[m]) and Dimension differs from Algebra without one.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeAlgebra / FreeAlgebraWithOne / FreeAssociativeAlgebra family
rubrics_metrics.description: FreeAlgebra(R, rank[, name]) constructs a free (nonassociative) algebra of given rank over R; FreeAlgebraWithOne produces a free algebra-with-one; FreeAssociativeAlgebra variants produce free associative algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional string names can provide generator names; printed GeneratorsOfAlgebra show symbolic generators. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: AlgebraByStructureConstants semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AlgebraByStructureConstants(R, sctable[, nameinfo]) returns a free left module A over division ring R with multiplication defined by structure constants table sctable; optional nameinfo prescribes canonical-basis names. It does not check that coefficients in sctable belong to R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis vectors of A correspond to sctable's basis ordering; examples demonstrate multiplication of basis vectors using returned algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: AlgebraWithOneByStructureConstants semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AlgebraWithOneByStructureConstants(R, sctable[, nameinfo], onecoeffs) is like AlgebraByStructureConstants but takes onecoeffs (coefficients vector over R) describing the multiplicative identity element w.r.t. defining basis, and returns an algebra-with-one; HasOne reflects presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows creating onecoeffs via Coefficients(B, One(A)) and constructing algebra-with-one from StructureConstantsTable.

rubrics_metrics.name: StructureConstantsTable format and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: StructureConstantsTable(B) returns a sparse structure constants table T for basis B: T is a list of length n+2 where first n entries are lists of length n; T[n+1] is 1, -1, or 0 for symmetric/antisymmetric/other; T[n+2] is zero of coefficient domain. T[i][j] stores product coefficients as [positions_list, coeffs_list].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described relation to structure matrices Mk with multiplication formula a M_k b^tr given; example shows representation for QuaternionAlgebra basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: EmptySCTable usage
rubrics_metrics.description: EmptySCTable(dim, zero[, flag]) returns a structure constants table describing trivial multiplication for an algebra of dimension dim with zero element zero; optional flag 'symmetric' or 'antisymmetric' indicates known (anti)commutativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as starting table to fill entries with SetEntrySCTable. Example demonstrates EmptySCTable(2, Zero(GF(5)), 'antisymmetric').

rubrics_metrics.name: SetEntrySCTable semantics and entry format
rubrics_metrics.description: SetEntrySCTable(T, i, j, list) sets entry describing product of i-th and j-th basis elements to list. If T is symmetric or antisymmetric the T[j][i] value is also set. list must be of the form [ck1, i_j_k1, ck2, i_j_k2, ...] where positions at odd list positions correspond to entries positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Odd-position entries must be compatible with T's zero element; rational numbers allowed and may be converted to appropriate prime field elements. Example usage shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: GapInputSCTable representation
rubrics_metrics.description: GapInputSCTable(T, varname) returns a string containing GAP commands using EmptySCTable and SetEntrySCTable that reconstruct T assigned to variable varname.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for serializing structure-constants tables into GAP input script. Example output shows assignments string with newline escapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestJacobi for structure-constants tables
rubrics_metrics.description: TestJacobi(T) tests whether structure constants table T satisfies the Jacobi identity v_i*(v_j*v_k) + v_j*(v_k*v_i) + v_k*(v_i*v_j) = 0 for all basis vectors with i ≤ j ≤ k (antisymmetry assumed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns true if Jacobi identity satisfied, otherwise returns a failing triple [i, j, k].
